messages:
Alex: heads up — nightly calibration sweep for int4/FP8 kernels showed a surprising throughput cliff when continuous batching is enabled.
Priya: ugh, repro on CI or just local?
Alex: repros on staging with mixed workloads (short + long). I ran a quick profile, looks like shape fragmentation causes a fallback to the FP16 large-tile kernel for certain slab shapes.
Cheng: paste of the trace output from the profiler:
```
kernel_select: fp8_packed_tile_32x128 -> fallback: fp16_tile_64x256
workload: seq_len=384, batch=5 (contiguous arrivals), pad_to=512
pad_waste=28%  (avg tokens per batch 393 -> padded to 512)
kernel_time_ms: fp8=2.1  fp16=2.0  (but fp8 path triggers extra copy + quant/dequant + alignment)
kv_copy_ms: 0.7 -> 1.4  (due to misaligned slabs -> split memcpy)
end_to_end_p95: 58ms -> 86ms
observed: throughput drops ~30% for mixed short/med tails when pad_waste > 20% and tile mismatch occurs
```
Priya: interesting that fp16 kernel_time looks similar in raw ms but end-to-end worse because of copies. so packing & kv behavior is the issue.
Lee: is this the same shape constraint we saw last quarter where kernels only accept stride % 64 == 0? if so the packer is creating fragmented slabs that exceed kernel shape constraints.
Cheng: yes, kernel has hard shape acceptance for the quantized path: packed_tiles must be multiples of 32x128. When continuous batching groups different seqs we end up with leftover fragment that forces a slower kernel + extra memcpy.
Sam: can we change batcher to be shape-aware? e.g., do a quick modulo group and avoid coalescing across alignment boundaries. Also a quick heuristic: if pad_waste > 20% and fragment_count > 1 then prefer smaller batch/flush.
Maria: +1. That would trade some throughput for lower latency p95. For PLG customers that care about p95 it's worth it.
Alex: FYI perf-bot already reported a regression on the calibration job this morning:
perf-bot: [perf/regression] calibrate-int4-fp8-nightly increased p95 by 18% (job id: cal-2026-03-12-47) :warning:
Priya: can we back out the latest quantization micro-optim that changed tile packing? IIRC that landed last week.
Cheng: I bisected — the regressor is the new quant packer that tried to reduce memory by packing heterogeneous seqs into one slab. It works for static batches but interacts poorly with continuous batcher padding.
Lee: short-term mitigation: force the packer to align to kernel tile when continuous_batching == true (config flag). Long-term: add a shape-aware coalescer that considers kv cache layout and memcpy costs.
Sam: I'll sketch a change: introduce pad_aware_grouping and a cost function: cost = pad_waste * alpha + memcpy_penalty * beta + kernel_pref_score. Use telemetry to tune alpha/beta.
Cheng: optimistic patch diff (pseudo):
```
if continuous_batching:
  for group in pending:
    if (group.pad_waste > 0.2 and group.fragment_count > 0):
      flush_group()
    elif (aligns_to_kernel_tile(group.shape) == false):
      try_repack_with_alignment()
```
Maria: also need to watch calibration quality — last run's MSE on logits for int4 increased slightly when we forced tighter packing. We must include eval loss delta in the rollout criteria.
Alex: agreed. for rollout plan: 1) short-term flag to force alignment (Lee) 2) add pad_aware_grouping in batcher (Sam) 3) add calibration check that blocks packing optim until drift < threshold (Cheng + Priya) 4) add telemetry metric for fragment_count + pad_waste in /console.
Priya: I'll add the telemetry rails and an alert if pad_waste > 25% on any model for > 5m.
perf-bot: [ci] cal-2026-03-12-47: job artifact uploaded -> /artifacts/cal-2026-03-12-47/profile.json
Alex: thanks. can someone take the quick flag patch for today? need it on staging before tomorrow's deploy window.
Lee: taking it. will open PR with toggle and a short test harness.
Sam: I have the grouping prototype, will push a branch and link in the PR review.
Cheng: I'll add the calibration regression check to the eval harness and run a few model sweeps overnight.
Maria: ping me if you want me to run customer workloads against staging after the flag is in.
Alex: perfect — will follow up in the PR. main takeaways: packing + continuous batching + kernel tile constraints -> fallback + memcpy -> end-to-end perf regression. fix with shape-aware grouping + telemetry + safety gating for calibration-driven packing. :white_check_mark:
